races.name: Lynn Lodge Stud Irish EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Come On Noddy
runners_data.spotlight: Profitable colt; E4,000 yearling; half-brother to 7f 2yo/9.5f AW winner Easily Convinced (inc France; RPR 71); dam French 1m2f 2yo winner (77), half-sister to 1m2f 2yo winner The Olympian; yard had recent 2yo winner; check market.

runners_data.name: Rejoinder
runners_data.spotlight: Space Blues colt; E92,000 foal, E82,000 2yo; closely related to 6f 2yo/1m Listed winner Thunder Beauty (RPR 109), half-brother to three winners inc Haku (prolific 1m4f AW; 101) and Quita (German 1m3f-1m6f); dam German 1m3f/1m4f winner; respected source and worth monitoring in the market.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Mann
runners_data.spotlight: Havana Grey colt; 160,000gns 2yo; dam 7f AW 2yo winner (RPR 76), half-sister to winners at 1m and 1m/8.7f, out of sister to 1m Group 1 winner Timepiece, half-sister to 1m2f 2yo Group 1 winner Passage Of Time; promising second in Naas barrier trial last month; very interesting debutant with Keane a notable booking.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.comment: E17,000 Cotai Glory filly, dam 2yo winner, makes plenty of appeal on paper
runners_data.spotlight: Cotai Glory filly; E17,000 yearling; dam 6f/7f winner (inc 2yo; RPR 90), out of maiden half-sister to 6f Listed winner Inyordreams and Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner Fire Eyes; best watched on debut unless the market speaks.

runners_data.name: Cleodolinda
runners_data.spotlight: Ten Sovereigns filly sent off at 8-1 on debut over C&D (yielding) and found just Matriarchal (who is closely matched with Hanney Boy) too good by 0.5l; dwelt at the start that day and made up lots of ground in the final furlong; should be more streetwise now and she's a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Away And Gone
runners_data.comment: Ardad filly, 40,000GBP 2yo, dam 1m winner, in good hands, market check advised
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off the 3-1 joint favourite on debut at Cork (5f, soft) but failed to run to market expectations; likely capable of better and interesting to see if her backers return, but can only be watched after that initial effort.

runners_data.name: Hanney Boy
runners_data.comment: 28-1 but ran a fine race on debut here over 5f, form boosted, 6f to suit, big chance
runners_data.spotlight: Promise both starts; stayed on well for a 5.5l second on debut at Cork (soft) and the third from that race won a maiden here since (Cleodolinda second); beaten favourite upped to 6f back at Cork (soft) when racing keenly; this stiff 5f could be ideal; leading claims.

runners_data.name: Desert Alchemist
runners_data.comment: 42,000gns Ghaiyyath colt, dam half-sister to talented stayer Carmers, may need further
runners_data.spotlight: Ghaiyyath gelding made a pleasing debut when a 2.75l third over 6f at Cork last month (Hanney Boy second), not quite getting home; the drop back to 5f should suit and he's a player.

runners_data.name: Queenofthewild
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and never landed a blow on debut over C&D, improvement needed
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off at 7-1 on debut at Cork but never landed a blow; 6.5l behind Hanney Boy that day and major improvement required to turn that form around.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.comment: Speedily-bred debutant hooded; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1, ran green and beaten 21l over 6f here on debut three weeks ago; may need more time.

races.name: Navan Racing Festival Early Bird Tickets On Sale Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Leading candidate with sustainable pace but concerning lack of wins since 2022 and recent poor form trend
runners_data.comment: Two runs so far this season leave him with a fair bit to find despite reduced mark
runners_data.spotlight: No win since 2022; hasn't looked like regaining the winning thread in three runs this term; behind The Highway Rat and Bodhi Bear at the Curragh (6f) latest; eased 2lb and the drop back to 5f is a plus, but the forecast rain is a concern.

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces major tactical disadvantage over 5f at this track despite solid recent Curragh effort
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time AW winner; both turf wins have come over this C&D on yielding and soft ground; pleasing seasonal return over 6f at the Curragh last month, not far behind Bodhi Bear; eased 1lb, yard in fine form and leading claims.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Another closer with wrong running style for course and distance, though Colin Keane booking adds slight appeal
runners_data.comment: Listed and Gr.2 winner was a 2.75l sixth behind Mission Central last time over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: High-class form for Clive Cox included a Group 2 win at Haydock in 2024; hasn't won since and last three runs for this stable not encouraging; mark sliding but needs to rediscover best; tongue tie tried now.

runners_data.name: Stag Night
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form and prominent style ideal for track, with solid record over course and distance
runners_data.comment: One win and five places from ten Curragh starts, good chance now after second last month
runners_data.spotlight: In fine form this season at the Curragh; third on seasonal reappearance (6f, heavy); 1.25l second behind Bodhi Bear on penultimate (5f, sft-hvy); won over 5f (soft) there on latest and the runner up has run well in Listed company since; 5lb rise fair and should be bang there again if the forecast rain materialises.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: Versatile ground performer with prominent style to suit, though 8lb rise since last win is concerning
runners_data.comment: Winner here in March and creditable run since in Listed; respected back in handicap class
runners_data.spotlight: Ground-versatile sort; won for the third time on seasonal return at the Curragh in March (5f, sft-hvy) off 8lb lower; not disgraced in Listed company at Naas; fine effort off revised mark back at the Curragh latest (6f, good) when ahead of The Highway Rat and Erosandpsyche; won his maiden here (6f) and should go well again.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: First-time blinkers after maiden breakthrough could provide further improvement at appealing weight
runners_data.comment: Top-rated, has C&D form, obvious chance but becoming expensive to follow; cheekpieces on
runners_data.spotlight: Gained breakthrough win at the tenth attempt in a C&D maiden (yielding) on latest in first time cheekpieces; now sports blinkers for first run in handicap company and talented claimer takes off a handy 5lb; can't discount.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Recent AW winner steps up in grade but prominent style and low weight offer compensation
runners_data.comment: Superior strike-rate on turf and was behind three of these on his last run here in March
runners_data.spotlight: Back to winning ways off 4lb lower at Dundalk on latest, making all to score by 0.5l; may find things tougher upped in grade off his revised rating (never won off a mark this high).

races.paceDynamic: Erosandpsyche will likely lead with Stag Night, Bodhi Bear, and Namiid pressing close behind, creating a competitive but manageable early gallop over this sharp 5f trip. Cuban Grey may also push forward from his low draw, while The Highway Rat and Kerdos will need to overcome their hold-up styles on a track that typically favors prominent racers. The presence of multiple prominent runners means the pace will be honest without being destructive. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners and those with early pace, as hold-up horses face a significant tactical disadvantage over 5f at Navan.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not suicidal, allowing prominent runners to maintain position.
scenarios.body: The front group stays together turning for home before the best handicapped horses kick clear in the final furlong. Hold-up horses struggle to make meaningful ground over the minimum trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Erosandpsyche gets an easy lead and the chasing pack fails to apply enough pressure.
scenarios.body: The veteran gets first run on his rivals and maintains his advantage to the line despite carrying top weight. Late closers are left with too much to do over the sharp 5f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably strong with multiple horses vying for the lead.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners tie up in the final furlong allowing The Highway Rat and Kerdos to storm home despite their tactical disadvantage. Track bias would need to favor closers unusually.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Winner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid's first-time blinkers provide significant improvement from his recent maiden success.
scenarios.body: The three-year-old builds on his breakthrough win with new headgear enhancing his focus and pace positioning. His light weight and upward trajectory prove decisive against older handicappers.

watchPoints.text: The Highway Rat and Kerdos both employ hold-up tactics that rarely succeed over 5f at Navan
Erosandpsyche's early position if he faces unexpected pressure from multiple prominent runners
Namiid's early positioning with first-time blinkers to gauge immediate improvement
Cuban Grey's ability to translate recent AW form to this higher grade on turf
Stag Night's fitness after 49-day break despite excellent recent course form

races.name: Book Your Hospitality Now For Navan Racing Festival Handicap

runners_data.name: Thurso
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong 6f-7f form but may struggle to get into contention from the back in this large field
runners_data.comment: Needs to get himself back on track and this is only his second attempt at 5f
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last year, at 6f and 7f; going was fast for last month's 5f Bath win on his final start for Richard Hughes; any ease might harm his chance on Irish debut.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and 5f specialist but poor recent form with eight straight unplaced efforts since July
runners_data.comment: Others preferred after finishing down the field at Navan after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-time winner is a 5f specialist; below his best in two starts last month and has been unplaced in eight races since a Tipperary win last July.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 352 days off the track makes him very hard to fancy despite decent historical form
runners_data.spotlight: Placed over 6f/7f in Britain two seasons ago; off for almost a year; hard to fancy against that background.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who looked uncomfortable on the bend at Listowel last time, which is a concern for Navan's configuration
runners_data.comment: Won over 6f at Naas last summer and fair fourth over 5f back there latest; blinkers added
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f at Naas last summer and fair fourth over 5f at the same venue on his penultimate start; looked ill at ease on the bend at Listowel last Sunday; not a big price on his last three starts; cheekpieces on now instead of usual tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with fade-in-finish warning who won his first turf race recently but carries top weight
runners_data.comment: Yet to hit form for this yard but handicapper giving him every chance; new headgear combo
runners_data.spotlight: Dual AW winner; highlight of British form when second to Big Evs in a Listed race at York in May 2024; rated 99 at his peak. gained his first turf success off 72 when making all in a 20-runner contest over an extended 6f at the Curragh on Wednesday; has a fixed 7lb penalty; an additional 2lb claimed this time; this stiff 5f should be fine for him.

runners_data.name: Alnofoor
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has thrived since returning from long layoff with back-to-back wins at Navan and Bellewstown
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from over four years off last year; has prospered in the second phase of his career, winning back-to-back at Navan (6f, heavy) and Bellewstown (5f, soft); continued in fine form when third in a 21-runner contest at the Curragh seven weeks ago; every chance if continuing in the same vein.

runners_data.name: Mickey The Steel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent course record (2 wins, 3 seconds from 9 visits) and solid recent form
runners_data.comment: Loves the mud and solid placed form over 6f/7f early in the season; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Has a decent record at this track, two wins and three seconds from nine visits; solid form this term except a moderate Curragh run over 7f; place chance now after last Sunday's third at Listowel; acts on good but best on soft or heavy.

runners_data.name: Viamonte
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 274 days since last run makes him a doubt despite good placing record this season
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in five maidens this year and also finished third in a C&D handicap last July; rider teamed up with his mother at Dundalk recently to provide her with a winning start to her training career.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Front runner wearing first-time cheekpieces after disappointing effort 12 days ago at Dundalk
runners_data.comment: Plenty to like about his close second behind Buddy Batt here in March
runners_data.spotlight: 5f maiden winner at two; confined to two runs last season; made a pleasing return at Dundalk in March, disappointed there 12 days ago; first time with cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trying a visor for the first time after running well when fifth in large field here recently
runners_data.comment: Latest of two turf runs offered some encouragement; visor now replaces cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in four of his eight AW starts, ran well when fifth of 17 over 6f here on latest; could make his presence felt if the addition of a visor helps; cheekpieces discarded.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with uneven form since August win, others look more dependable in this competitive heat
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Bellewstown last time; back to her winning mark so considered
runners_data.spotlight: Uneven form since winning over this trip at Cork last August; respectable fourth at Bellewstown, down the field at this venue last time; others are more dependable.

runners_data.name: Polar Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with slow start issues who was third here in April but poor last time when always near back
runners_data.comment: Three years since last win; running well this term but slow starts are killing him
runners_data.spotlight: Slow starts have been an issue this season, including when third here in April, 1 1/4l behind Al Laochmor; poor effort when always near the back at Fairyhouse on Friday.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and 15-race maiden who showed encouragement when third at Curragh in 20-runner field
runners_data.comment: Recent C&D third could go well given a level break
runners_data.spotlight: 15-race maiden, placed five times; last month's Curragh third was an encouraging display in a 20-runner field; will not need to improve much to win a handicap of this standard.

runners_data.name: Three Sixteen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with modest form who failed to make impact in claimer on seasonal debut
runners_data.comment: Three ordinary maiden runs last season; hooded on return for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form last season, failed to make an impact in a claimer on stable/seasonal debut; not one of the more obvious candidates.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose four wins all came at this track with most recent success off 4lb lower mark
runners_data.comment: Course specialist but tends to need her first run after an absence
runners_data.spotlight: All four of her wins have come over sprint distances at this track, most recently last October off a 4lb lower mark; should be better for last month's outing here; needs to reverse the form of that race with Happy Henry and Jazzit.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent recent form who is probably better over 6f but should handle stiff 5f
runners_data.comment: Just 1lb higher than when runner up at Sligo on penultimate, may need softer ground
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent form in his last five races; probably best over 6f but he should be fine with this stiff 5f; definitely not without a chance following his third placings at this venue and Fairyhouse; has early-season form linked to Alnofoor; change of headgear now.

runners_data.name: An Laochmor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who transferred excellent AW form to turf with course second six weeks ago
runners_data.comment: In form on AW, good run on return to turf at Navan, fourth in this last year off 6lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: Transferred his excellent AW form (4211) to turf when second over C&D six week ago; chance in this company is underlined by his victory over Jordan Breeze at Dundalk in April; shares a consistent recent profile with that rival and Alnofoor.

runners_data.name: Astute Power
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with ordinary form except close third here last October, plenty to prove after poor return
runners_data.spotlight: Ordinary form other than a close third of nine in a C&D maiden at Navan on soft last October; in rear at the Curragh on return, plenty to prove a a result

runners_data.name: Plushy
runners_data.note: Front runner concerning that she was well beaten in weak maidens on last two starts
runners_data.comment: Enjoys good; excuses for Naas flop as fly leapt the stalls; contender eased in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on first two starts in 5f maidens last year at Bellewstown (good) and Cork (good to firm); also placed twice at Dundalk in January; concerning that she was well below her best at Down Royal nine days ago.

runners_data.name: Verified
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fade-in-finish warning who is a 21-race maiden with dented confidence after poor runs
runners_data.comment: 0-18 on turf, best runs at Cork, no impact on stable bow latest, Keane takes over now
runners_data.spotlight: 21-race maiden; has occasionally shown winning potential; placed three times last year for his former trainer; two moderate runs this season have dented confidence in his ability to score.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 135-day break with record when fresh suggesting he needs this run
runners_data.comment: Won off 2lb higher last season, poor at Dundalk when last seen in Jan', might need this
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 2lb lower at Tipperary last season (5f, good); failed to beat a rival when last seen at Dundalk in January; record when fresh suggests he might need this run.

runners_data.name: Jackie Jump Up
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to step up significantly from low-key handicap debut ten days ago
runners_data.comment: 2l behind Baiana latest, new headgear combination tried, in the mix if handles ground
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort at two when placed over 6f at this track; needs to step up from a low-key handicap debut at Fairyhouse ten days ago.

runners_data.name: Jordan Breeze
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has become reliable this season with recent Cork win after placing behind An Laochmor
runners_data.comment: Fine run on return and again when a close second latest, same mark, in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Has developed into a reliable sort this season; second to An Laochmor at Dundalk and also runner-up to Alnofoor at Bellewstown before a well-deserved Cork win; apprentice has a good record on him; has stronger credentials than most

races.paceDynamic: Lethimfly and Plushy are the confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead in this competitive 23-runner handicap. With both horses needing to be handy, they'll set an honest gallop from the start, creating a strong pace that should stretch the field. The large field and stiff 5f course at Navan means those who get into early trouble or are too far back will struggle to make up ground. This pace setup and course configuration strongly favours prominent racers and those who can travel just behind the leaders, as hold-up horses will find it difficult to weave through traffic and make late headway in such a competitive field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not suicidal, allowing prominent runners to stay in touch
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will stretch out the field perfectly for those tracking the leaders, who can then pounce in the final furlong. Hold-up horses will be caught too far back in this large field to mount effective challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Speed Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lethimfly or Plushy get an uncontested lead and the pace becomes more moderate
scenarios.body: The front runners will have enough left in reserve to hold off late challenges, especially with first-time cheekpieces helping Lethimfly's concentration. The large field will struggle to organize a coordinated assault on the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Behind
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the leaders come back to the field
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up a finish for the closers, though they'll need clear runs through the traffic. Only the best-handicapped hold-up horses will be able to capitalize as most will be too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If there's significant trouble in running or the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: The large field creates multiple opportunities for interference, potentially eliminating several fancied runners. This opens the door for an outsider who gets the right trip and avoids the carnage.

watchPoints.text: Lethimfly is the likely pace-setter but his disappointing Dundalk effort 12 days ago raises questions about current form
Watch for traffic problems in the home straight with 23 runners and several hold-up horses needing clear runs
An Laochmor has proven course form and successfully transferred his AW ability to turf six weeks ago
Polar Bear's slow start issues could be crucial in a large field where early positioning is vital
Mickey The Steel's excellent Navan record (2-3-0-1 from 9 runs) gives him a significant course advantage

races.name: Navan Handicap

runners_data.name: Greek Flower
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on long losing streak but 46 days since last run freshens her up for this tactical test
runners_data.comment: Often placed but hard to be confident on account of her lengthy losing streak
runners_data.spotlight: On a long losing streak (since October 2023) but shaped well on several occasions, including on seasonal debut at Leopardstown; less encouraging run at Gowran dents confidence in her prospects of adding to her tally.

runners_data.name: Ocean's Breath
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Colin Keane aboard, only 2 days since last run but proven at this trip and track
runners_data.comment: Ready winner over 6f on AW; raced alone and on wrong side when fav for Naas handicap
runners_data.spotlight: 6f Dundalk winner in April; showing when favourite for a premier handicap at Naas can be excused; got warm beforehand and then had to race alone; won a 7f rated race comfortably at Fairyhouse on Friday; drops back in trip and carries 7lb penalty now.

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing to overcome unconvincing recent form, visor applied for this assignment
runners_data.comment: Most recent run this term was a step in the right direction and down to a career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time Curragh winner over 5f/6f on varying ground; has also scored at this track; recent form is unconvincing; trainer may have a better chance with the apprentice-ridden Collective Power.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario, headgear added and fair recent Dundalk form translates
runners_data.comment: Beaten less than a length when third on AW; missed break when well-held fourth at Navan
runners_data.spotlight: Won 7f maiden for Aidan O'Brien; fair AW run in March when beaten less than a length in third over 6f; missed break when well-held fourth at this venue; needs to reverse the form of last Sunday's Listowel clash with I Bid You Ajou and Aurora Nova.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needed clear run last time, proven hat-trick winner at this distance when conditions suit
runners_data.comment: Couldn't get in the clear until too late when beaten just over 2l at the Curragh last time
runners_data.spotlight: Came good last summer with a quick-fire Fairyhouse hat-trick over 6f; touched off at Naas three starts ago; denied a clear run until too late in a premier handicap at the Curragh two weeks ago; generally dependable sort was one place in front of Aurora Nova at Listowel last Sunday.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with stronger AW record than turf, visor fitted for return to grass racing
runners_data.comment: Posted a career-best RPR when winning over 6f here in April; Chester run forgiven
runners_data.spotlight: Beat I Bid You Ajou at Dundalk in April; his AW record (5-30, placed nine times) is much stronger than turf (1-22, placed three times); only limited appeal with those statistics in mind.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on AW but showed reversal of form with Clonmacash suggests improvement possible
runners_data.comment: Always respected here; close up behind Clonmacash on his last visit in April
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time AW winner; was close up in third behind Clonmacash at Dundalk in April; second there on latest, reversing form with Clonmacash in the process; has the merit of being a C&D winner; definite chance for 10lb claimer who has made the frame in three of the five Irish races she has ridden in.

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying low weight with claiming jockey, good comeback run at Bellewstown boosts confidence
runners_data.comment: Dual 5f winner at Bellewstown last term and good comeback run at same track in April
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough over 6f two seasons ago; her three wins last term were all over 5f, two of them at Bellewstown, where she had a good comeback run in April; closely matched with Aurora Nova on last Sunday's running at Listowel.

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: Prominent style but well below best in two runs this term, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Best form at Cork but ran well over C&D last term; better for recent comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins for Kieran Cotter came at Cork (6f-1m); a long way below best in two races this term.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing return to form, 22 days since last run provides freshness advantage
runners_data.comment: C&D winner, raised 3lb for close third at Naas on latest, this is a stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown signs of a return to his best; backed up a second placing over 5f at Naas with a third over 5f at this venue, a showing that gives him an edge over Alfred Tennyson.

races.paceDynamic: Ocean's Breath will dictate from the front with Alfred Tennyson and Gerrit's Gem providing early company before settling behind. The pace will be genuine but not frantic over 6f on good ground, with the main body of hold-up horses including Greek Flower, Jon Riggens, I Bid You Ajou, Clonmacash, Collective Power, Aurora Nova and Nouvel Espoir tracking in behind. This should create a strong gallop that will suit horses with tactical pace who can position close enough to strike, while penalizing those needing significant ground to make up. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners and those with early pace over pure hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean's Breath maintains a solid gallop without going too fast early
scenarios.body: The even pace allows prominent runners to travel well and kick clear in the final furlong while hold-up horses struggle to close the gap. Early positioning proves decisive with those tracking the pace having the tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favors Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean's Breath goes too fast early or gets pressed hard by Alfred Tennyson and Gerrit's Gem
scenarios.body: The hot pace sets up perfectly for the large group of hold-up horses who can finish strongly as the early leaders tire. Late runners with good finishing kicks benefit from the collapse up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Up Front
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean's Breath faces more pressure early than expected from multiple prominent runners
scenarios.body: The pace becomes stop-start as runners jostle for position early, creating a sprint finish that favors horses with natural speed regardless of running style. The race becomes more about class and speed than tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early Becomes Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean's Breath is allowed to dictate a steady pace with minimal early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop turns the race into a 2f sprint where natural speed and finishing kick matter most. Hold-up horses with turn of foot benefit while one-paced prominent runners get swamped.

watchPoints.text: Ocean's Breath could get a soft lead if Alfred Tennyson and Gerrit's Gem don't provide early pressure
I Bid You Ajou needs clear running room in the straight after being denied last time out
Greek Flower's market support will indicate connections' confidence after her long losing run
Jon Riggens and Collective Power both trained by Edward Lynam who may favor one over the other
Aurora Nova carries bottom weight with claiming jockey which provides significant weight advantage

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Hill Of Tara Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Hotazhell
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario but 245 days off raises fitness concerns despite Group 1-winning ability
runners_data.spotlight: Ended his 2yo campaign with a Group 1 win, beating Delacroix in the William Hill Futurity; no wins last year, but managed a fine third in the Irish 2,000 Guineas and a fair fourth in the Irish Champion Stakes (1m2f); too keen when attempting 1m4f in the Arc; can win races at four and this appeals as a suitable starting point if his fitness holds up.

runners_data.name: Wemightakedlongway
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose Oaks form gives her a class edge but headgear change suggests trainer concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's best performances came in Group 1s when runner-up in the Irish Oaks at the Curragh (1m4f, good) and very close fourth in the Prix de l'Opera at Longchamp (1m2f, very soft); flopped on reappearance at Cork; Haydock third was reassuring; however, best at 1m2f-1m4f.

runners_data.name: Norwalk Havoc
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader whose Leopardstown success doesn't guarantee Navan effectiveness against stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: Looks on a stiff mark, while trip and draw pose questions; could do with plenty of rain
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner at 7f/1m, the last two at Listed level; Leopardstown specialist; considerably inferior to stablemate Hotazhell.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: Promising three-year-old whose prominent style suits but lacks the proven class of his main rivals
runners_data.spotlight: Won Curragh maiden on debut (7f, good); later ran with credit in Group 2 juvenile events won by the Prix du Jockey Club principals, Constitution River and Hawk Mountain; yet to advance that profile in races at the Curragh and Leopardstown this season; premature to write off; hood added to tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Hazdann
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 434-day absence makes him hard to assess despite previous promise
runners_data.spotlight: 7f maiden winner at two; not seen again after a promising fourth behind Henri Matissse on seasonal debut last year; worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Bubble Gum
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits but two moderate runs this season suggest she's regressing from her Cork Listed win
runners_data.spotlight: Finished midfield in French and German Oaks in 2024; Listed winner at Cork for Paddy Twomey on Irish debut; failed to build on that; two moderate runs this season; needs big improvement in first-time blinkers.

runners_data.name: Lemsairbat
runners_data.note: Reliable hold-up horse whose recent Listed placings prove he belongs at this level despite poor strike rate
runners_data.spotlight: Poor strike rate of 1-19 but has run plenty of solid races in defeat; twice runner-up in Listed races this term, so not out of place here; chased home stablemate Sindria at Gowran last time, with Subsonic back in third.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Group 1 juvenile form gives him claims if the pace sets up correctly
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner at Goodwood; best juvenile form when staying on from off the pace to take fourth behind Pierre Bonnard in Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud (1m2f, very soft) in October; shaped as if he needed the race when fourth of seven in a Listed event at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on return; eased when beaten in Derby Trial at Lingfield; should be competitive now.

runners_data.name: Flushing Meadows
runners_data.note: Prominent runner held by Geryon at Leopardstown and struggling with this year's form
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two small-field Group 3 races at two; question to answer on this year's form; held by Geryon on Leopardstown running; last of five behind Constitution River in the Dee Stakes; stablemate Isaac Newton is more appealing.

runners_data.name: Lady Lilac
runners_data.note: Prominent handicapper whose 88 rating makes her outclassed in Listed company
runners_data.spotlight: Fair handicapper; 88-rated filly has found things too demanding on her first two attempts in this grade.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Front runner whose debut second to top-class Minnie Hauk remains her best form reference
runners_data.spotlight: Second to the top-class Minnie Hauk on debut at Leopardstown in 2024 (1m, soft); off the mark on her fourth and final start of 2025 in a 1m2f Curragh maiden; achieved a clear career-best when third at Gowran a month ago, closely matched with Lemsairbat.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better suited to shorter trips based on his juvenile winning pattern
runners_data.comment: Looked well suited by 7f at two, faced stiff task on seasonal debut, place chance at best
runners_data.spotlight: Looked well suited by 7f when winning twice at two; vulnerable at this level on the evidence of two runs this term.

races.paceDynamic: Norwalk Havoc and Subsonic will contest the early lead with five prominent runners (Hotazhell, Wemightakedlongway, Geryon, Bubble Gum, Flushing Meadows) creating traffic congestion behind the leaders. The pace should be honest but not destructive with two genuine front-runners ensuring no crawl. Hold-up horses Hazdann, Lemsairbat, Isaac Newton and Summer Is Tomorrow face the challenge of finding racing room in the straight as the prominent brigade converges. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can secure a clear run while avoiding both the pace duel up front and the traffic problems further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but manageable between Norwalk Havoc and Subsonic
scenarios.body: The five prominent runners get first run on the leaders while the hold-up horses struggle for racing room in a bunched finish. Hotazhell and Wemightakedlongway use their class advantage from ideal positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hot Pace Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Norwalk Havoc and Subsonic go too fast early in their battle for the lead
scenarios.body: Both leaders weaken significantly in the final furlong allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past late. Hazdann and Isaac Newton benefit most from the strong early gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of Norwalk Havoc or Subsonic gets an uncontested lead while the other drops back
scenarios.body: The surviving leader gets soft fractions and kicks clear of the field before the closers can respond. Norwalk Havoc's Listed wins suggest he's most capable of pulling this off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Creates Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too slow early creating a sprint finish from the back
scenarios.body: The entire field converges in the final two furlongs with racing room at a premium. The best horse on pure ability regardless of position wins in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Norwalk Havoc and Subsonic must be monitored for an unsustainable early pace that could set up the race for closers
Hotazhell needs to show early sharpness after 245 days off to secure his preferred prominent position
The five prominent runners risk creating a wall effect that blocks the hold-up horses' finishing kicks
Hazdann's market support will indicate connections' confidence after his 434-day layoff
Isaac Newton's position turning for home will determine if he can unleash his proven late kick

races.name: Darley Irish EBF Kooyonga Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who may struggle if the pace is too strong, returning after 28 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Second in a 1m Listed race at Killarney last August; aimed very high in the Matron Stakes and now has her sights lowered after contesting a 7f Group 3 event at Leopardstown four weeks ago; this extra furlong may prove closer to the optimum trip.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's hold-up mount looks perfectly suited to the expected strong pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Looked smart when making a winning debut over 1m at Naas in March; a combination of inexperience and trouble in running proved her undoing in a 1m fillies' Group 3 at the Curragh early last month; has something to prove now after a lifeless display over 1m2f at the same venue last time.

runners_data.name: Quebec
runners_data.note: Prominent style may work if pace collapses but recent form suggests she's outclassed at this level
runners_data.comment: Useful form in Germany, failed to make an impression behind City Of Memphis on Irish debut
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice in Pattern races in Germany last year; has failed to make an impression in Pattern races won by the smart City Of Memphis; detached last of 12 in the Leopardstown race in which Sindria finished ninth.

runners_data.name: La Fogata
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with proven 1m form who should benefit from the anticipated strong gallop
runners_data.spotlight: Useful form over 1m as a juvenile; beaten 5l in a six-runner Curragh Group 3, strong at the line when landing Punchestown maiden; heavy ground a possible excuse for a poor run on final start for Ger Lyons; finished in front of well-fancied stablemate Eretria when second in a Listed race over an extended 1m2f at Naas on first outing for this team.

runners_data.name: Yellowstone Lake
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 254 days off which raises fitness concerns despite natural pace-setting style
runners_data.spotlight: Went close on Leopardstown debut last July and then fourth of ten behind the brilliant Diamond Necklace over 7f at the Curragh; beat the useful Emmeleia in a maiden at Dundalk in September; looks almost sure to improve her official rating of 89, if she has trained on satisfactorily.

runners_data.name: White Sand Beach
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter but maiden status and poor recent form make her vulnerable when pace pressure builds
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in all four maiden attempts, including behind La Fogata last season and stablemate Drop Dead Gorgeous at Naas in March; last of 12 in a Group 3 event at the Curragh; hard to fancy at this level following an unplaced handicap run on latest.

runners_data.name: Fingerpaint
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 231 days off, suited to strong pace if fit enough
runners_data.spotlight: Debut 7f winner at the Curragh early last season; fair third in Group 3 event at Tipperary last August, having been badly hampered turning in; probably unsuited by heavy ground when failing to make an impact at Leopardstown on her final start.

runners_data.name: Fast Tara
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated pace-setter whose job may be simply to ensure honest gallop before fading
runners_data.comment: Rallied for a close second last time; should go well again but this ground may not suit
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice in handicaps this term; only one win from 26 starts; faces a huge task in this company.

runners_data.name: Sindria
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly matches expected race shape, recent Group 2 run suggests she's sharp
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in a Group 2 event at the Curragh a fortnight ago; had previously stamped herself as an improving filly with two Gowran wins, the second of which was in this grade, earning a 3lb penalty; 100-rated filly is joint top-rated on official ratings with two of the younger generation.

runners_data.name: Sanctijude
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making big step up in class after maiden breakthrough
runners_data.comment: Maiden with plenty of good runs; place claims at least back in maiden company
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent in maidens and handicaps before breakthrough win at Gowran on her tenth start; 81-rated filly faces a big task in this grade.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing blinkers, meets stablemate Duckadilly on poor terms
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive handicapper on heavy ground late last season; best of her three runs this season when third in the Irish Lincoln; meets stablemate Duckadilly on 16lb worse than handicap terms; blinkered for the first time.

races.paceDynamic: Yellowstone Lake, White Sand Beach, and Fast Tara will ensure a strong gallop from the off, with all three having confirmed front-running styles. This sustained pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the mile trip on good ground. The relentless tempo will suit hold-up horses like Drop Dead Gorgeous, La Fogata, and Sindria who can finish strongly when others tire. This race shape clearly favours closers and hold-up performers who can unleash their finish when the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed pace-setters maintain a genuine gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo will stretch the field and create perfect conditions for hold-up horses to finish strongly when others weaken. Drop Dead Gorgeous and La Fogata can time their runs to perfection as the early leaders fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Yellowstone Lake, White Sand Beach, or Fast Tara drop out early leaving insufficient pace
scenarios.body: The reduced tempo will favour horses that can travel closer to the pace and kick when the race becomes tactical. Duckadilly and Quebec can position prominently and have more left in the tank for the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Sustained Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters settle into a steady rhythm rather than flat-out racing
scenarios.body: This even tempo will suit versatile types who can adapt their position and still have a strong finish. La Fogata and Sindria can travel well within themselves before unleashing their closing kicks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fast Early Brutal Pace
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders engage in early speed duels creating unsustainable fractions
scenarios.body: The suicidal tempo will set up an extreme closer's race where only horses held up furthest back can finish. Fingerpaint and Syzygy from the rear can pick up the pieces as everything else stops.

watchPoints.text: Fast Tara and White Sand Beach could compromise each other if they engage in early speed duel
Yellowstone Lake's fitness after 254 days off may affect her ability to sustain the early pace
Drop Dead Gorgeous and Ryan Moore's positioning in the early stages will indicate their confidence level
Fingerpaint's readiness after 231 days absence could determine if she can capitalize on the pace setup
Quebec's early position will reveal whether connections think she can compete at this level

races.name: Cusack Hotel Group Family Raceday July 11th Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Spinning Web
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 295-day break faces impossible task from rear in likely uncontested pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Poor in this sphere last time after a couple of falls chasing; isn't well-treated here
runners_data.spotlight: Has lost way over hurdles and fences; won off 2lb lower at Dundalk (1m4f) in 2023 but 0-9 on turf on the Flat and others arrive in better form.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tendency to fade late, needs to be closer to Proleek Prince but lacks early speed to challenge
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner is 0-11 on turf on the Flat; well below best over hurdles on last two starts and ran poorly when last seen on the level at Dundalk; hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Kevin The Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching yards and adding tongue-tie, but 0-9 record for previous trainer suggests limited ability
runners_data.comment: 0-8, hinted he needed further than 1m2f last season, drop in trip a query here; blinkered
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 for Jessica Harrington; showed promise on a couple of occasions off higher marks last year but two runs this year were poor; new yard now and tongue tie goes on; stamina to prove up in trip.

runners_data.name: El Regalo
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden returning to blinkers but showed nothing in recent starts and faces wrong race shape
runners_data.comment: Down the field in two recent Flat outings, hurdles form is unconvincing; cheekpieces now
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose maiden yet to trouble the judge in either code; soundly beaten on last two Flat starts and over hurdles on latest; drops in grade and blinkers return, but hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Deluca Chop
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form with 1lb rise after good second at Roscommon, needs pace to develop
runners_data.spotlight: Knocking on the door on the AW earlier this year; fine run on return to turf when a 1.75l second at Roscommon (Mapa behind); nudged up 1lb but should be thereabouts again; visor goes on.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Prominent runner off 228-day break with poor recent form, unlikely to challenge early pace despite style
runners_data.comment: 0-26 over hurdles, has run well here on the Flat, may need this after 194 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 2-38 on turf; no win since 2022 and was pulled up over hurdles at Sligo 26 days ago on return from a break; hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose sole win came here at this trip, but needs strong pace to be effective from rear
runners_data.comment: Won here last September and excuses on latest; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came off this mark at Down Royal last September (1m5f, good); hasn't really fired this season and beaten 8.75l back at Down Royal latest (2m, good), but has gone well over this C&D before so not discounted.

runners_data.name: Proleek Prince
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly positioned to lead unchallenged, recent 8-length defeat suggests beatable despite tactics
runners_data.comment: Yet to hit form this year, tries this longer trip again
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins in 2024 but has been in the handicapper's grip since; not a bad run at Fairyhouse latest (1m2f, good) but still beaten 8l and didn't look to be crying out for this longer trip; down in grade but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Mapa
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden with solid recent third at Roscommon, needs pace development but has tactical speed for finish
runners_data.comment: Second over 10.5f on AW in November; no impact on ine previous attempt over this far
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden but has run well in defeat, including when a keeping-on 3l third of 16 on seasonal return at Roscommon on latest (1m4f, yld-sft); worth a go at this longer trip on that evidence; big player off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with recent win, dropping in trip but has tactical ability if pace becomes genuine test
runners_data.comment: Veteran recorded ninth win at Sligo last time; up 8lb but in the mix.
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran gained the ninth win of his career when bolting up at Sligo on penultimate (1m6f, yld-sft); raised 8lb and couldn't follow up at Listowel (2m, good); drop back in trip a plus and has run well here before; place shout.

runners_data.name: Ethereal Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse well below career-best form, 46-day break and poor recent runs suggest limited threat
runners_data.comment: Below best twice this term but handicapper giving her every chance; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Standout effort a 2.75l third at Killarney last July off 7lb higher but nowhere near that level in two runs this season; beaten 17.5l at Gowran on latest; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Sarmiento Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor turf record, 0-4 on grass and remains well above winning mark
runners_data.comment: C&D winner in September but doesn't appear to be in anything like the same form currently
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f AW winner is 0-4 on turf; recent showings at Dundalk not encouraging and remains 7lb above sole win; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fade tendency, out of form and step up to 1m5f showed no improvement last time
runners_data.comment: Nothing of any substance since 2023 Killarney win; 9lb wrong; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Won on heavy ground at Killarney (1m) in 2023 but no joy since; out of form this term and step up to 1m5f didn't elicit improvement at Leopardstown latest; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Mr Mills
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 198-day break with tongue-tie, modest record and long absence major concerns
runners_data.comment: Little of note in light campaign in recent years; belatedly tried in a tongue-tie here
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time winner, including here over 1m2f (soft) but hasn't scored since 2023; fine effort when last sighted at Dundalk in November; off since and has a modest record when fresh but worth a market check.

runners_data.name: God The Highness
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse 0-10 on turf but placed twice over similar trips, 2lb drop in handicap provides hope
runners_data.comment: Has shown some ability in low-grade staying handicaps on the Flat, early days hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10 on turf on the Flat; placed twice last season, over 1m6f here (soft) and over 13.5f (gd-yld) at Sligo; 2lb lower now and shaped okay in a Limerick maiden hurdle latest; cheekpieces on; could go well.

runners_data.name: Idomything
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fade tendency, won off 2lb lower but needs much softer ground than current good surface
runners_data.comment: Winner over 1m4f on soft ground at Bellewstown in October; well beaten since
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 2lb lower at Bellewstown last October (12.5f, soft); not a bad effort when midfield at Roscommon latest (1m4f, yld-sft); rain would boost chance.

races.paceDynamic: Proleek Prince will dominate the early lead with no serious challengers for pace, creating a sustainable tempo over this 1m5f trip. Jazz Forever and Lariat may sit prominent but neither has the early speed to challenge Proleek Prince's position, allowing him to dictate fractions without pressure. The large field of 16 will settle into a strung-out formation behind the lone leader, with the majority of hold-up horses tracking in midfield and rear. This uncontested pace scenario heavily favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to Proleek Prince and kick when the tempo lifts in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Proleek Prince maintains an easy lead without pace pressure through halfway
scenarios.body: The lone leader can control the race completely and prove difficult to peg back over this staying trip, while prominent horses like Jazz Forever get first run at him. Hold-up horses face an impossible task trying to make ground from the rear against an unchallenged leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If the field closes up behind Proleek Prince turning for home and multiple horses challenge
scenarios.body: The race becomes a proper test of stamina where horses with tactical speed can strike, benefiting those who travel well in behind like Desert Friend and Mapa. Proleek Prince may find the sustained pressure tells on his stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Proleek Prince sets too slow a pace and the field remains bunched
scenarios.body: The race turns into a sprint finish where class and turn-of-foot matter most, suiting hold-up horses with tactical speed. Fresh horses off breaks like Lariat or improving types like Deluca Chop can capitalize on the lack of early pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Jazz Forever or Lariat decide to challenge Proleek Prince for the early lead
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle develops that sets up the race for strong finishers who can pick up the pieces. The early speed duel compromises the front-runners and opens the door for closers with stamina.

watchPoints.text: Proleek Prince dictating an uncontested pace through halfway could make this race a procession with front-runners dominating
Jazz Forever and Lariat failing to take up prominent positions early would leave Proleek Prince completely alone on the lead
Desert Friend and Mapa tracking closer than usual in midfield could signal connections expect a stronger pace than likely
The large field of 16 spreading out behind a lone leader could create traffic problems for hold-up horses in the straight
Deluca Chop and God The Highness getting prominent positions despite hold-up styles would indicate tactical changes worth noting

races.name: Cusack Hotel Group Family Raceday July 11th Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form, Colin Keane booking suggests confidence, 9 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Decent run at Dundalk last month off 8lb higher AW mark so has to be of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Two solid runs since return from winter break; 4l third at Dundalk (1m4f), then 0.5l behind Jurality when third at Down Royal (Synchronize fourth); 2lb rise for that seems a touch harsh, but place claims again.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is the only pace angle, 7lb claimer is a concern but gets uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: Recent second on turf but that's more his surface; 0-9 on AW and yet to place
runners_data.spotlight: Knows how to win and shaped as though her turn was near when running on well for second at Leopardstown (ahead of Jurality and Felicity Smoak); big chance if she backs that up off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 345-day break, likely needs the run despite promising past form
runners_data.spotlight: 1-23 on turf; beaten 7l in this last year and just 1lb lower now; off since poor run over hurdles at the Galway festival; may need this run.

runners_data.name: Felicity Smoak
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with improving flat form, 5lb claimer reduces weight burden significantly
runners_data.comment: Poor form over hurdles on winter ground, showed promise over 1m2f at Fairyhouse last June
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort yet on the Flat when a 3.75l sixth of 20 at Leopardstown (1m5f, good) on return from 139 days off, denied a clear run (1.5l behind Eastern Wind); sharper for that, same mark here and should be thereabouts with smoother passage.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with concerning finishing fade pattern, poor recent form makes him hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Money for him over C&D last week when beaten around 6l; up in grade and more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 73 at Limerick last summer (12.5f, good); poor form since, though his penultimate run at Roscommon wasn't devoid of promise; not as good there on latest but now drops into 0-60 company and is on a dangerous mark.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent recent form, closely matched with several rivals on previous meetings
runners_data.comment: Recent Leopardstown third ensures he makes the shortlist here
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden running consistently well in defeat this year; closely matched with a couple of these rivals on Leopardstown third on penultimate and on latest Down Royal second (2m, good); nudged up 3lb but should continue to give a good account.

runners_data.name: Just Another Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling on turf, 7lb claimer helps but poor turf record is concerning
runners_data.comment: Slipped up at Dundalk on final 2025 start, best form at 1m4f/1m6f, this may be inadequate
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f AW winner is 0-15 on turf; beaten a head over 1m6f here last October on soft off 2lb lower; 1m was inadequate on seasonal return at Gowran; should come on plenty for that and not discounted back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Edge Of Darkness
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with finishing fade pattern, missed break last time suggests alertness issues
runners_data.comment: Four-time winner in Britain but nothing like that form for current yard; 5lb wrong
runners_data.spotlight: 4-20 on turf but hasn't won since 2023; not a bad run over 2m at Listowel (2m, good) after missing the break latest; more needed back in trip, but positive rider booking.

runners_data.name: Nita
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 184-day break with fade pattern, stable form is poor recently
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins at 1m2f-1m3f in Germany but bar a Dundalk third last November, hasn't really threatened for this yard; off since December and returns with stable in decent fettle, so market check advised.

runners_data.name: Cahir Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut, cheekpieces first time suggests connections seeking improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap debutante didn't show a whole lot in maidens at 9.5f-1m4f on varying ground; off since October and sports cheekpieces; best watched.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well last time, 18lb weight advantage could be significant at this level
runners_data.comment: Mild hurdles promise at times but of limited appeal back on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden produced one of his better efforts on latest when not far behind a couple of these rivals at Down Royal (2m, good); place shout if he backs that up, but overall profile suggests that's not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and maiden with stamina doubts, 3lb claimer helps but limited winning ability shown
runners_data.comment: Overall form not too encouraging; tries this new trip but pedigree doesn't give much hope
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden showed a glimmer of promise at Bellewstown in April but poor twice since; yet to prove she stays this trip and much more needed to get her head in front.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fade pattern, poor turf record and slow start tendencies are major concerns
runners_data.comment: Modest performer and only making up the numbers here
runners_data.spotlight: Not the easiest to win with, as his 2-63 record on turf illustrates; never involved after a slow start in a QR race at Listowel latest; unproven at this trip.

runners_data.name: Appian Way
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from hurdles, 116 days off and poor recent form make him hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: One of his two hurdle wins came at this track; has been soundly beaten on recent starts
runners_data.spotlight: Flat maiden has won two over hurdles; out of form in that sphere this year and while he has gone well here before, he's hard to fancy on recent showings; tame effort again over hurdles at Clonmel on Friday.

runners_data.name: Creative Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with fade pattern, 3lb out of handicap and stamina doubts for this trip
runners_data.comment: Recent Sligo third was his first time in the frame, younger rivals have stronger claims
runners_data.spotlight: Long-standing maiden showed a bit more when third at Sligo (10.5f, yld-sft) on latest when 5lb wrong; 3lb out of the handicap here and stamina to prove for this trip; others appeal more.

races.paceDynamic: Eastern Wind is the only confirmed front runner in this 15-runner field and should get an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop over this stamina-testing 1m5f trip. Creative Dancer may show some early speed but typically fades, leaving Eastern Wind to dictate throughout the early and middle stages. The large field of hold-up horses will create a cavalry charge from the back in the straight, but the lack of genuine pace pressure should allow the leaders to maintain their advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the finishing kick from the rear may come too late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Eastern Wind gets soft fractions and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: She can maintain her advantage through superior positioning while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic or arrives too late. Her recent Leopardstown second suggests she's ready to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their preferred scenario with a sprint finish where class and finishing kick matter most. Mephisto's recent form and Jurality's consistency become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Eastern Wind goes too fast early or gets pressured by Creative Dancer
scenarios.body: The leaders weaken dramatically in the final furlong, creating a messy finish where positioning and luck matter more than ability. Fresh horses from midfield can capitalize on the chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and an improver finds significant improvement
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced or returning horse hits the frame at big odds through fitness or untapped potential. The handicapper may have gotten the weights wrong.

watchPoints.text: Eastern Wind must be monitored early - if she goes too fast trying to use her pace advantage, she could set it up for the closers
Mephisto and Jurality are closely matched on recent form - whichever gets the cleaner passage in the straight should finish ahead of the other
Several horses carry fade-in-finish warnings (God Of Thunder, Edge Of Darkness, Nita, Talking Tough, Appian Way, Creative Dancer) making the pace scenario critical
The 7lb claiming riders on Eastern Wind, Just Another Eagle, and Talking Tough could impact their mounts' chances in a competitive finish
Folly Beach and Nita return from long breaks (345 and 184 days respectively) - watch for market confidence or lack thereof
